rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a useful performance baseline before testing more complex profile, encoder, image, or fusion choices. config_001 tests a minimal RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline, which will establish reference validation accuracy and F1 for later comparisons with multiprofile settings, learned RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion. It is the best first use of budget because it is simple, low-risk, and creates a necessary anchor for isolating the effects of other design decisions.

The only completed run is RNA-only, single-profile PCA (acc 0.485, F1 0.464), leaving uncertainty about whether the RNA representation is limiting. config_004 changes only the RNA encoder to scVI while keeping single-profile and no aggregation/fusion, so it cleanly tests representation quality. This minimal comparison is more informative than adding multiprofile, image, or fusion now, because it reduces uncertainty about a core design choice with low confounding under a limited budget.

RNA-only singleprofile results show scvi_n200 outperforming pca_n2000 (accuracy 0.520 vs 0.485; F1 0.498 vs 0.464), but with only two RNA encoders tested the representation choice remains uncertain. config_007 tests scgpt with the same singleprofile setting and no aggregation or fusion, isolating the effect of RNA representation. This is the best next experiment because it completes a clean encoder comparison before adding profile, aggregation, image, or fusion complexity; if scgpt is stronger it changes future multimodal choices, and if not it confirms scvi as the RNA baseline and allows the next experiments to focus on profile/aggregation or image modality.

Existing evidence shows that, among RNA-only single-profile models, scvi_n200 is the strongest representation (accuracy 0.520, F1 0.498), while pca_n2000 and scgpt are weaker. There is no evidence yet for multiprofile settings. config_005 tests whether multiple profiles with a simple avgpool aggregation improve over the best single-profile RNA model while keeping the RNA encoder fixed and avoiding more complex choices like transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising RNA representation, isolates the profile/aggregation question with minimal added complexity, and will clarify whether multiprofile modeling is worth further investment before testing fusion or image modalities.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with scvi_n200 and avgpool reaches 0.650 accuracy, well above the single-profile RNA baselines, but the contribution of aggregation is still untested. config_006 keeps the best current RNA encoder and profile setting fixed while changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, directly clarifying whether transformer aggregation improves multiprofile representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction while isolating an important design choice, and the result will guide whether future multimodal experiments should use avgpool or transformer aggregation.

The completed runs show that multiprofile RNA with scvi_n200 is much stronger than singleprofile RNA, while avgpool and transformer aggregation are nearly equivalent, but there is still no evidence that the image modality is useful. config_011 tests an image-only baseline in the promising multiprofile regime using a simple standard encoder (resnet50) and simple aggregation (avgpool), without adding fusion. This is the best next experiment because it isolates the image representation question, provides the baseline needed to interpret future multimodal/fusion experiments, and avoids committing budget to a more complex multimodal or ViT-L setup before knowing whether image features contain signal.

Existing evidence shows a large gain from single-profile to multiprofile RNA using scvi_n200 (accuracy 0.520 to 0.650, F1 0.498 to 0.628), while avgpool vs transformer aggregation is nearly identical and image-only resnet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile helps broadly or specifically requires the scvi representation. config_002 tests pca_n2000 with multiprofile and avgpool, directly comparing to config_001 for the profile effect and to config_005 for the encoder effect. This isolates representation and profile setting without adding image/fusion complexity, making it a high-information next step before investing in multimodal extensions.

RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 is the strongest evidence so far (about 0.65 accuracy/F1), but image-only evidence is sparse and weak: resnet50 multiprofile avgpool scored only 0.328 accuracy. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality has useful signal with a stronger encoder before committing budget to multimodal fusion. config_014 tests this by changing only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping the same multiprofile and avgpool setting as config_011. This cleanly isolates the effect of image representation, avoids introducing multiple untested changes at once, and helps decide whether image features are worth fusing in later experiments.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200, reaching about 0.65 accuracy and 0.63 F1, while image-only multiprofile avgpool is much weaker, with imagenet_vit_l slightly better than resnet50 in both accuracy and F1. No multimodal configuration has been tested yet. config_036 keeps the known strong RNA setting (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) and the slightly better known image setting (imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool), then tests the simplest fusion rule, concat. This directly clarifies whether adding image information via concat improves over the strong RNA-only baseline without confounding the result with untested transformer image aggregation or a more complex weighted fusion. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest RNA evidence while establishing a clean multimodal baseline before exploring transformer aggregation or weighted fusion.

The strongest evidence is config_036, the multimodal multiprofile scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l avgpool concat model, which outperforms all RNA-only and image-only baselines. RNA-only multiprofile scvi also showed a small transformer-over-avgpool advantage, but aggregation has not yet been tested in the best multimodal setting. config_038 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, isolating whether a more expressive profile aggregator improves the top configuration. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction while cleanly testing an important design choice under limited budget.
